sourcedFrom: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 (2026)
cleanIntro: The 77/22 is Ruger's rimfire bolt rifle, made in .22 LR, .22 WMR and .22 Hornet, and it feeds from a rotary magazine that sits flush in the stock. Ruger covers it in its 77-Series book, which also covers the 77/17, 77/44 and 77/357. The safety is a three-position selector on the tang: SAFE at the rear, LOAD-UNLOAD in the middle, FIRE at the front. Ruger's field strip is the magazine and the bolt out, then the bolt taken down to its breech block, bolt sleeve and firing pin. The bolt sleeve assembly itself is permanent and is never taken apart, and neither is the magazine.

steps.title: Safety to LOAD-UNLOAD, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and keep your finger out of the trigger guard. If the cocking piece is sticking out of the back of the bolt sleeve, the rifle is cocked: move the safety selector to the middle LOAD-UNLOAD position. Then take the magazine out of the bottom of the rifle. Taking the magazine out does not unload the chamber, so the rifle can still fire a round that is already in it.
steps.quote: Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction! If the firing pin is cocked, put the safety in the “load-unload” position, then, remove the magazine.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 1, p.24
steps.warn: Removing the magazine does not prevent the rifle from being fired!

steps.title: Open the bolt and look in the chamber
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt back, gently enough that a live round comes out without being flung. Then look into the chamber yourself and make sure it is empty. A rimfire case is small, and a cartridge pulled back slowly can drop into the magazine well instead of leaving the rifle, so look rather than trust the ejection.
steps.quote: OPEN THE BOLT AND CHECK TO BE CERTAIN THAT THE CHAMBER IS EMPTY.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 2, p.24

steps.title: Empty the magazine with a pencil eraser
steps.action: If cartridges are left in the rotary magazine, push the top one lightly down and forward and it comes out. For rimfire rounds, press the top cartridge down with the eraser end of a pencil while you push it forward. Never use another cartridge as the tool. Put all the ammunition away from where you will clean.
steps.quote: For rimfire cartridges, use the eraser end of a pencil to press the top cartridge down while pushing forward.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — To Unload Rifle and Magazine, step 7, p.19
steps.warn: Do not use a loaded cartridge as a “tool” to strip cartridges from the magazine.

steps.title: Bolt out: handle up, press the bolt stop, slide it out
steps.action: With the safety still on LOAD-UNLOAD, lift the bolt handle up and draw the bolt back. The bolt stop is on the left side of the receiver. Press it down lightly, a thumbnail is enough, and pull the bolt out of the back of the receiver.
steps.quote: Lift the bolt handle up. Depress the bolt stop on the left side of the receiver. Remove the bolt from the rifle.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 3, p.24

steps.title: Turn the bolt sleeve clockwise to its takedown position
steps.action: Hold the bolt by its handle. Looking at it from the rear, turn the bolt sleeve clockwise to the position Ruger shows in its Figure 10. This lets the cocking piece go forward and takes the striker tension off the breech block, so the parts at the front can come out.
steps.quote: While holding the bolt handle, rotate the bolt sleeve clock-wise (as viewed from the rear of the rifle) to the position shown in Figure 10.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 4a, p.24

steps.title: Line up the breech block pin and push it out
steps.action: Turn the breech block at the front of the bolt until the head of its retaining pin lines up with the larger holes in the bolt body. Then put a thin pin through the small hole on the opposite side and push the retaining pin out. The alignment has to be exact: if the pin will not move, turn the breech block a little and try again rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: Push out the breech block retaining pin by inserting a pin through the small hole on the side opposite from the larger hole. The alignment must be precise to remove the retainer.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 4b–4c, p.24

steps.title: Breech block out the front
steps.action: With the retaining pin out, slide the breech block assembly forward and out of the front of the bolt. It carries the extractor, so handle it gently and put it in your parts tray.
steps.quote: Remove the breech block assembly by sliding it forward out of the bolt
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 4d, p.24

steps.title: Pin the cocking piece back through the disassembly hole
steps.action: Find the disassembly hole in the striker and cocking piece assembly. Put a small pin or a suitable nail into it to hold the cocking piece to the rear. Ruger asks for one as close to the hole's size as you can find and at least 2 inches long, because you will use it as a lever on the cocking piece when the bolt goes back together. Leave it in.
steps.quote: Insert a small pin (or suitable nail) into the “disassembly hole” in the striker/cocking piece assembly to hold it in the rear position
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 4e, p.24

steps.title: Unscrew the bolt sleeve, firing pin out
steps.action: With the pin holding the cocking piece back, unscrew the bolt sleeve and take the bolt sleeve assembly out of the bolt. The firing pin can now be lifted out of the bolt sleeve assembly. The bolt sleeve assembly stops there: it holds parts under great spring pressure and is never taken apart.
steps.quote: Unscrew the bolt sleeve (Figure 12). Remove the bolt sleeve assembly. Firing pin can now be removed from the bolt sleeve assembly
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 4f, p.24
steps.warn: The bolt sleeve assembly is intended to be a permanent assembly and should not be disassembled.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench now: the rifle in its stock, the empty magazine, the bolt body, the breech block, the bolt sleeve assembly with your pin still in it, and the firing pin. That is the field strip Ruger's cleaning section starts from. The stock, trigger, sear, safety and bolt stop stay in the rifle for a routine clean.
steps.quote: Disassemble (field-strip) the rifle to the extent described on pages 23 - 24.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, step 1, p.30

steps.title: Rod in from the chamber end, all the way through
steps.action: With the bolt out, put the cleaning rod in at the chamber end and push it firmly until the patch or brush comes out of the muzzle. Do not pull it back while a brush or patch is still in the bore, because it can bind. Use the correct size patches and brushes, and do not use any that are dripping with solvent or oil.
steps.quote: With the bolt removed, insert the cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel and push firmly so the patch or brush emerges from the muzzle.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: Solvent patch, brush, then dry patches
steps.action: Push-pull a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times. Then run a solvent-wetted brush the full length of the bore as many times as it takes to get everything out of the bore and chamber. Dry it with clean patches and look through it; if it is still fouled, brush it again. Finish with dry patches through the bore and chamber.
steps.quote: Complete the cleaning by dry-patch wiping the bore and chamber.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Toothbrush on the bolt parts and the receiver
steps.action: Wipe every surface you can reach inside the receiver with a clean solvent-wetted patch. Use a solvent-wetted toothbrush on caked dirt on all the bolt parts, the breech block and extractor included, and on the parts of the receiver a patch cannot reach. Then wipe the solvent off with patches or a cloth. Ruger warns against caustic and acetone-based cleaners and against automotive or paint-stripping products.
steps.quote: Use the solvent-wetted toothbrush to dislodge caked dirt from all parts of the bolt assembly and from surfaces inside the receiver that can’t be reached with a patch.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, step 3, p.30
steps.warn: NEVER USE AUTOMOTIVE OR PAINT STRIPPING PRODUCTS TO CLEAN YOUR FIREARM.

steps.title: A very light coat of oil, a drop on the moving parts
steps.action: Wipe all the surfaces, inside and out, with a very light coat of oil; oil collects dirt, so use it sparingly. A drop on the bolt parts, the trigger pivots, the safety, the bolt stop and the magazine latch is all they need. Keep the bore clear of oil and grease before the rifle is fired.
steps.quote: A drop of oil applied to the bolt assembly components, the pivot points of the trigger mechanism, the safety, the bolt stop, and the magazine latch, will work into all the parts that need lubrication.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, step 4, p.31

steps.title: The magazine stays together
steps.action: The rotary magazine is cleaned whole and is never taken apart. Ruger warns that putting it back together wrong, or getting the rotor spring tension wrong, can cause a dangerous malfunction. If the magazine gives you trouble, Ruger's answer is a new magazine.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Magazine Inspection and Care, p.29

steps.title: Soak, shake out, then test the rotor
steps.action: Soak the magazine in a solvent that will not rust its metal parts or harm its plastic box. Then shake it hard, with the loading opening pointed away from you, to get the solvent and dirt out. Test the rotor afterwards: load one cartridge, press firmly on the side of the case and let go quickly. The cartridge must snap fully up into the feeding position. If cleaning does not fix the rotor, do not use the magazine. Take the test cartridge out.
steps.quote: After the magazine has been soaked in solvent to loosen foreign matter, be certain to shake it vigorously (with the loading opening away from you) to remove solvent or residue from within the magazine.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Magazine Inspection and Care, p.29

steps.title: Wipe the stock clean
steps.action: After the rifle is back together, wipe all the solvent, oil and preservative off the stock. Ruger asks you to test any cleaner on a hidden spot first, because some can harm the stock and the metal finish. If the rifle is going into storage for a long time, clean it thoroughly and wipe the metal again with preservative oil.
steps.quote: Reassemble the rifle and carefully wipe all solvent, lubricating, and preservative preparations from the stock.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Care and Cleaning, step 5, p.31

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Before going deeper: a lost spring is never substituted
deepSteps.action: The trigger, the safety selector and the bolt stop are all under spring tension. Work over a covered bench so a plunger that jumps is caught, and keep each part in a box as it comes out. If a spring or plunger is lost, get the correct part; never use a substitute.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger suggests a shallow nap rug or an old coarse blanket on the bench, and photos on your phone as you go.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: If a spring or plunger becomes lost do not use a substitute.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly — Warning, p.24

deepSteps.title: Stock off: rear screw out, trigger guard out
deepSteps.action: With the bolt and magazine out of the rifle, take out the rear mounting screw in the trigger guard. Swing the back of the trigger guard out of the stock to clear the trigger, unhook the guard from the receiver and lift it out. If your stock has a magazine well liner, take out the front mounting screw and the liner next; if it does not, only the front mounting screw comes out.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger notes the 77-Series has many stock types; the trigger guard and liner steps apply only to stocks that have the magazine well liner.
deepSteps.quote: a. Remove the rear mounting screw in the trigger guard. b. Swing the rear of the trigger guard out of the stock to clear the trigger.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 5, p.25

deepSteps.title: Lift the barrel and receiver out of the stock
deepSteps.action: Very carefully lift the barrel and receiver together out of the stock. Do not scrape, sand or re-bed the stock while it is apart: Ruger will not rework a stock that has been altered.
deepSteps.quote: VERY CAREFULLY lift the barrel/receiver assembly from the stock.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 5d, p.25

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The barrel stays in the receiver
deepSteps.action: The barrel is threaded into the receiver and only the factory takes it out. Leave it in place. The one exception Ruger names is older .22 LR, .22 Magnum and .17 HMR rifles made before 11/13/2009 and serial number 703-58030, whose barrel is held by two retainer screws and a retainer; Ruger's book gives that removal for those rifles only, with the retainer screws going back to 15–20 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.quote: Barrels are threaded into the receiver and should not be removed except by the factory.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 6, p.25

deepSteps.title: Trigger out: safety on FIRE, hold the trigger, press out the pin
deepSteps.action: Put the safety selector on FIRE. Hold the trigger in place and press out the trigger pivot pin. The trigger is under spring tension, so keep hold of it as the pin clears, then take out the trigger and the trigger/sear spring.
deepSteps.prose: The trigger/sear spring sits over a dimple in the trigger, which is where it goes back.
deepSteps.quote: While holding the trigger in place, press out the trigger pivot pin.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 7, p.25
deepSteps.warn: The trigger is under spring tension and must be controlled during removal

deepSteps.title: Sear out: pin out, receiver upside down, slide forward
deepSteps.action: Press out the sear pivot pin. Turn the receiver upside down and slide the sear forward, and it drops out through the top slot in the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the receiver upside down and slide the sear forward. The sear will drop out of the top slot in the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 8, p.25

deepSteps.title: Safety out: hold the selector, slide the retainer up
deepSteps.action: Turn the safety selector so its upper section sits fully over the middle of the receiver tang. Hold it there with thumb and forefinger and slide the retainer up out of the receiver. A spring and plunger push on the selector, so keep hold of it until the retainer is clear. Then lift out the selector and take out its detent and detent spring.
deepSteps.quote: While holding the safety selector in place with a thumb and forefinger, slide the retainer up out of receiver.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 9, p.25
deepSteps.warn: Failure to contain the safety selector will result in the spring and plunger "jumping" out

deepSteps.title: Bolt stop out: press the plunger, lift it off the pivot
deepSteps.action: Press the bolt stop plunger in with the tip of a jeweller's screwdriver and lift the bolt stop off its pivot. The plunger and spring are under tension and will jump out if you let them, so cover them. Then take out the plunger and its spring. That is as far as Ruger's book takes the rifle apart.
deepSteps.quote: Depress the bolt stop plunger (with the tip of a jewelers screwdriver blade or similar tool) and remove the bolt stop from the pivot.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® 77-Series Bolt-Action Rifles (77/17®, 77/22®, 77/44®, 77/357™) (PM085) — PM085 / 77/17 — Disassembly, step 10, p.26
deepSteps.warn: This spring and plunger are under spring tension.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bolt out; the rod goes in from the chamber end
Push through until the patch or brush comes out of the muzzle; do not reverse it in the bore
No patches or brushes dripping with solvent or oil
Solvent patch several times, then a solvent brush the full length of the bore
Dry patches, look through it, brush again if still fouled
Finish with dry patches through the bore and chamber

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Solvent patch over every reachable surface in the receiver
Toothbrush on the bolt body, breech block, extractor and bolt sleeve
Solvent wiped off with patches or a cloth
Never use caustic or acetone-based cleaners, or automotive or paint-stripping products
A very light coat of oil; a drop on the bolt parts, trigger pivots, safety, bolt stop and magazine latch
Do not take the bolt sleeve assembly apart

cleaning.name: ROTARY MAGAZINE
tasks: Do not take the magazine apart
Soak in a solvent safe for its plastic box and metal parts
Shake it out hard, loading opening pointed away from you
Test the rotor with one cartridge; it must snap fully up
A magazine that cleaning does not fix is not used

cleaning.name: STOCK & EXTERIOR
tasks: Test any cleaner on a hidden spot first
Solvent, oil and preservative wiped off the stock
Never alter the stock bedding
Long storage: cleaned thoroughly and metal rewiped with preservative oil

reassembly: If the deep strip was done: bolt stop plunger and spring in (the step flats on the plunger matching the flats on the bolt stop), plunger pressed, bolt stop back on its pivot.

Safety detent and spring into their hole, selector set with its upper section over the middle of the tang, retainer slid into the dovetail from the top with its notch lined up with the sear pivot pin hole.
Sear in from the top, rear end (the end with the hole) first, swung up and slid until its hole lines up, then the sear pivot pin.
Trigger/sear spring over the dimple in the trigger, trigger in with the spring on the sear's dimple, trigger pivot pin in while you hold the trigger.

Barrel and receiver into the stock, pushed to the rearmost position, with no pivot pin sticking out of either side; magazine well liner and front mounting screw in (65 in-lb maximum); trigger guard hooked in at the front and swung into place; rear mounting screw snug by hand.
Bolt: firing pin into its slot in the bolt sleeve assembly, sleeve slid into the bolt handle from the rear and screwed clockwise to Ruger's Figure 11 position.
Breech block into the front of the bolt, holes lined up, retaining pin pushed in with its flats lined up with the slot in the breech block.

Bolt sleeve turned counterclockwise until the cocking piece drops into the small notch in the bolt; then the pin or nail comes out. The breech block should rock freely about 1/16 inch each way; if it does not, put the pin back and check the retaining pin is fully seated.
Only when the bolt is correctly assembled: safety on LOAD-UNLOAD, bolt into the receiver, then the empty magazine in until it clicks.
fncheck: With no ammunition in the chamber or the magazine and the rifle pointed somewhere safe: with the magazine out, work the bolt a few times and feel it run smoothly. Close it, put the safety on FIRE and pull the trigger; listen for the firing pin click, and repeat twice more. Close the bolt again without pulling the trigger. On SAFE (rearmost) the trigger must not click and the bolt handle must not lift. On LOAD-UNLOAD (middle) the trigger must not click but the bolt must work. On FIRE (forward) the trigger clicks and the bolt works. Then, with the bolt open and the safety on LOAD-UNLOAD, push an EMPTY magazine in until it latches with a click, and pull on it without pressing the release; it must stay in. If any check is doubtful, Ruger sends you to a competent gunsmith or its customer service before the rifle is used.
